ADJOURNED EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE
  MEETING MINUTES
  JULY 30, 2018

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN MITCHELL called the meeting to order, the time being 7:03 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Judy Mitchell
Susan Brtis
Patricia Harik
Lou Persichina
Vicki Shinn
Carrie Silvano

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF JUNE 25, 2018
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE JUNE 25, 2018 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
None

CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT MONTHLY
UPDATE
Korey Bradbury and Susan Cordone from California Water Service Company distributed
update fact sheets and reported that the project was on schedule. MEMBER SHINN thanked
them for training the construction workers about how to interact safely around equestrians.
She encouraged them to put up safety signage on the Palos Verdes Landfill where vehicles
and materials were being staged for the project. MEMBER SILVANO noted that the safety
signage is also needed for all the dog walkers using this loop trail.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JULY 30, 2018  1
 Nancy Wildman, 34 Pony Lane, reported that the decision to use the Palos Verdes Landfill for
staging was recently made and that signage was in the approval stages. Susan Cordone
indicated that they expected the signs to be approved on July 31, 2018 and sent to their sign
company for prompt production and installation on the Palos Verdes Landfill. Ms. Wildman
also noted that she would be printing notices to place in holders at the various entry sites for
the Palos Verdes Landfill loop trail.

Korey Bradbury stated that a portion of the east side of the Palos Verdes Landfill would be
used as the staging area, along Crenshaw Boulevard, including the former LA County
Recycle Center. In addition, the loop trail was being re-routed through the middle of the
landfill so that there would be no conflicts. MEMBER SHINN requested that the new
temporary trail be checked, and if necessary, have any holes leveled.

Ms. Wildman reported that Gil Houle, Peter Weber Equestrian Center operator, had been
notified about the re-routed loop trail on the landfill. She also stated that there would be an
article regarding this trail detour in the upcoming PVPHA Dispatch. The Community Services
Director will meet with the Portuguese Bend National Horse Show organizers and determine
whether parking for horse trailers may have to be relocated on the Palos Verdes Landfill.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

DRAFT CITY CELEBRATION PROMOTIONS
The Community Services Director reviewed the draft promotional items that the Betty’s
Foundation organizers had produced for the Equestrian Committee’s review. They included a
2-sided, envelope-sized, flyer and a large poster. Committee Members did not have any
corrections and made positive comments on the quality of the promotional materials.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

EQUINE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE
MEMBER SHINN reported that LA County Animal Care & Control Department will hold a
Level 1 Equestrian Response Team (ERT) course on Saturday, September 8, 2018 from 9:00
a.m. to 1:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers. In addition, she indicated that a horse
chipping clinic would be held at the Peter Weber Equestrian Center sometime in September.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

PROPOSED EXPANSION OF CHANDLER PARK HORSE ARENA
The Community Services Director reviewed the staff report noting that due to two mature
trees located near the Chandler Park arena, that the maximum that this horse arena could be
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JULY 30, 2018  2
 expanded was approximately 20 feet at an in-house cost of approximately $12,800. He
indicated that if the project was completed by a local contractor, that it may cost an additional
$10,000 to $12,000. An email in support of the 20-foot expansion from MEMBER DEAN-
PORTER was reviewed by the Equestrian Committee. MEMBERS SHINN and SILVANO
concurred with MEMBER DEAN-PORTER’S assessment.

CHAIRMAN MITCHELL indicated her concern about where the funding would come from for
such a project, noting that the City had previously spent large amounts of money improving its
equestrian facilities.

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO RECOMMEND THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MAKE A
  RECOMMENDATION TO CITY COUNCIL TO EXPAND THE CHANDLER PARK
  HORSE ARENA BY 20 FEET AT A COST OF APPROXIMATELY $12,800.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

ERNIE HOWLETT PARK JUDGES BOOTH COMPLETION UPDATE
The Community Services Director indicated that representatives from the Peninsula
Committee – Childrens Hospital were at this meeting and would address the free bay window
offer that was made by their Horse Show Manager last year. Organization President, Sue
Wilkinson, apologized for the misunderstanding and provided two quotes from a contractor
who volunteered at their show. A vinyl window system would cost approximately $1,800 and
an aluminum window installation would cost approximately $1,400.

CHAIRMAN MITCHELL recommended that staff contact the Alan Pre-Fab Buildings, who
constructed the horse show judges booths for recommendations and to put this item on the
next meeting agenda. Los Serranos Award Circuit horse shows coordinator, Becky Martin,
recommended that the temporary steps be replaced with permanent steps.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS

  MEMBER SILVANO reported that the Howlett Trail fencing just west of the Hawthorne
  Tunnel needed replacement.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JULY 30, 2018  3
   MEMBER SHINN expressed concern about the tall stakes holding waddles in Howlett
  Park.

  Audience member, Jennifer Chatterfee, a Rancho Palos Verdes resident boarding a
  horse on Masongate Drive, informed staff that brush clearing measures were needed
  on the Ferncreek and Valmonte Trails.

B.  The Community Services Director reported that the Rolling Hills Road
  equestrian/pedestrian crossing safety concerns would be addressed at the August 15,
  2018 Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting at 6:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council
  Chambers.

C.  CHAIRMAN MITCHELL reviewed the letter from Mayor Huff to the Palos Verdes
  Peninsula School Board regarding the City’s concerns about the changes to the
  Equestrian Riding Team at Peninsula High School.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT UPDATE – Monthly

B.  EQUINE EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN UPDATE – Monthly

C.  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK JUDGES BOOTH COMPLETION – August 27, 2018

D.  PROPOSED EXPANSION OF CHANDLER PARK HORSE ARENA – August 27, 2018

E.  MANURE COMPOSTING METHODS – August 27, 2018

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL ADJOURNED THE MEETING TO
JULY 30, 2018.

The meeting adjourned at 7:56 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
